title: Clementine Sorbet
changes_from_base: Fresh clementine juice, blended raw with sugar and a little corn syrup, replaces the mango purée and lime; no cooked syrup.
summary: Pure winter sunshine: freshly blended clementine juice, sugar and a pinch of salt churned into a bright, sweet-sharp sorbet.

ingredients.item: light corn syrup or glucose syrup
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Peel
steps.text: Peel the cold clementines and pull them into segments, picking off any loose white threads. Purée: blend the segments in two or three batches for about 30 seconds each, until liquid.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Press the pulp through the sieve into the jug until you have 900 ml of juice; drink any extra.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Rinse the blender, then blend the juice with the sugar, corn syrup and salt for 30 seconds, until no grains of sugar remain.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: If the fruit was not cold to start with, refrigerate the juice for 2-3 h.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn for 20-25 min; eat it soft straight away or freeze for 4 h for neat scoops.

tips: Chill the clementines before peeling so the juice is cold and ready to churn.
Seedless clementines save time; pick out any pips before blending.
Serve in hollowed clementine shells for a party.
storage: Keep covered in the freezer for up to 1 week; sorbet turns icy after that. Soften for 10 min before scooping.
